Meanwhile modern systems lean on a cache layer to avoid repeated disk reads; the database stays calm while hot rows sit in memory, ready instantly. A good cache turns slow queries into fast ones without rewriting a single application line.

However correctness is harder than speed. Every cached value can drift from the truth stored on disk, so teams pick an invalidation rule: expire by time, evict by size, or delete on write; each choice trades freshness against load. A stale cache can break billing, so measure hit rates and watch what the cache misses.

Along with that, many shops map hot data into RAM at start up; though that trick works it risks stinky data if any row shifts without alarm, so audit which is truly known as an actual fact.

Finally plan for failure: when that fast layer dies, traffic must still reach storage safely, or your weekend is done.
